rules: displayRoot = (root + transpose - capo) mod 12; the bass moves the same way (data-model 2.5).
The spelling key is the key of the region the chord starts in (fallback the global key; no key = sharps), moved by (tonic + transpose - capo) mod 12.

Flats when the moved key's relative major tonic is one of F Bb Eb Ab Db Gb (major tonic t, minor tonic t + 3); otherwise sharps. 6 accidentals: Gb major / Eb minor flats, F# major / D# minor are never produced.
A sharps key spells every chromatic chord with sharps (C major: A#, not Bb) - the binding data-model rule.
Slash bass: '/' + the moved bass spelled with the same key; a bass equal to the root is not written.
No chord (root null) = 'N.C.' at every transpose and capo.

Key display: '<Tonic> major|minor'; transpose t != 0 -> '<moved> (original <key>, +t|-t)'; confidence < 0.5 appends ' (uncertain)'; the written key adds the instrument's semitones (mod 12) to the concert tonic, spelled the same way.
Capo shape: the chord lowered by the capo (displayRoot with capo). Open shapes by root pitch class and quality (research R-14 table; the bass is ignored); everything else is a barre shape.

Capo advisor: for c in 0..7, open = open-shape time / non-N time; rank by open - 0.02 c, exact ties by the lower capo; top three; shapeKey = global key lowered by c (and moved by the transpose); fewOpenShapes when the best open < 0.5; open rounded to 4 decimals.
Shortcut: transpose t in 1..7 -> capo t; t = -5 -> capo 7; otherwise none.
